questions.stem: In the Indian parliamentary executive, the nominal and real heads of the Union are respectively
options: the Prime Minister and the President
the President and the Prime Minister
the Vice-President and the President
the President and the Council of Ministers as a whole
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: To be eligible for election as President of India, a person must, among other things, be
options: at least 35 years of age and qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha
at least 30 years of age and a member of the Rajya Sabha
at least 40 years of age
at least 35 years of age and a member of the Lok Sabha at the time of election
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The President of India is elected by
options: direct election on universal adult franchise
proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote, through secret ballot
the members of the Lok Sabha only
a simple majority of the electoral college
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT included in the electoral college for the election of the President?
options: Elected members of the Lok Sabha
Elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies
Members of the State Legislative Councils
Elected members of the Delhi and Puducherry Assemblies
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Regarding the impeachment of the President under Article 61, which one of the following is correct?
options: The sole ground is proved misbehaviour or incapacity
Only elected members of Parliament take part
It requires a simple majority of both Houses
The sole ground is violation of the Constitution, and both elected and nominated members of Parliament participate, while MLAs do not
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The President of India tenders his resignation to
options: the Vice-President
the Chief Justice of India
the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
the Prime Minister
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: If the offices of both the President and the Vice-President fall vacant at the same time, who acts as President?
options: The Prime Minister
The Chief Justice of India, or in his absence the senior-most Supreme Court judge
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
The Attorney General
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The President is bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers by virtue of which amendment, and which amendment allows one reconsideration?
options: 24th Amendment made the advice binding; 44th allows reconsideration
44th Amendment made the advice binding; 42nd allows reconsideration
42nd Amendment made the advice binding; 44th Amendment allows the President to return a matter once for reconsideration
42nd Amendment allows reconsideration; 44th made the advice binding
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following pardoning powers removes both the sentence and the conviction of an offender?
options: Commutation
Remission
Reprieve
Pardon
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: With reference to the pardoning power, which one of the following is correct?
options: The President alone can pardon a death sentence and a court-martial sentence
The Governor can pardon a court-martial sentence
The Governor can pardon a death sentence
Neither the President nor the Governor can pardon a death sentence
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Governor of a state is
options: directly elected by the people of the state
appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President
elected by the State Legislative Assembly
appointed by the Chief Minister
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following is a matter of the Governor's constitutional discretion?
options: Assenting to every bill passed by the Assembly
Appointing the Chief Justice of the High Court
Reserving a state bill for the consideration of the President and recommending President's Rule
Declaring a financial emergency in the state
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: An ordinance promulgated by the Governor under Article 213 must be laid before the state legislature and ceases to operate unless approved within
options: two weeks
three months
six months
six weeks of its reassembly
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about the Vice-President of India is correct?
options: He is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and is elected by all members of both Houses of Parliament, elected and nominated
He is elected by both Houses of Parliament and the State Assemblies
He can be removed only by impeachment for violating the Constitution
He must be a member of the Rajya Sabha at the time of election
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: For how long can the Vice-President act as President when a vacancy occurs in the office of the President?
options: Three months
A maximum of six months
One year
Until the next general election
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following about the appointment of the Prime Minister is correct?
options: The PM must be a member of the Lok Sabha at the time of appointment
The PM is elected directly by the Lok Sabha
The PM is appointed by the President, and if not already a member of either House must become one within six months
The PM is appointed by the Vice-President
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The maximum size of the Union Council of Ministers, and the minimum size of a State Council of Ministers, are respectively
options: 20% of the Lok Sabha; no minimum
10% of the Lok Sabha; ten members
15% of both Houses; fifteen members
15% of the Lok Sabha; twelve members (91st Amendment, 2003)
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Prime Minister is the ex-officio Chairman of which one of the following?
options: The NITI Aayog
The Finance Commission
The Union Public Service Commission
The Election Commission
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Attorney General of India, the highest law officer, is
options: a whole-time salaried government servant barred from private practice
appointed by the President, must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge, and can take part in Parliament but cannot vote
appointed by the Chief Justice of India
a member of the Union Cabinet
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Governor and must be qualified to be
options: a Supreme Court judge
a district judge
a High Court judge
a member of the State Public Service Commission
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India requires the Prime Minister to furnish information related to decisions of the Council of Ministers to the President of India?
options: Article 78
Article 74
Article 75
Article 81
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The total number of members in the Union Council of Ministers in India shall not exceed
options: 10% of the total number of members of the Parliament
15% of the total number of members of the Parliament
10% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The President of India is elected by an Electoral College comprising the elected members of which of the following? 1. Both Houses of Parliament 2. The Legislative Assemblies of States 3. The Legislative Councils of States 4. The Legislative Assemblies of NCT of Delhi and Puducherry. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
options: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
1, 2 and 4
3 and 4
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which provision of the Constitution of India provides that the President shall not be answerable to any Court in India for the exercise of the powers of his office?
options: Article 53
Article 74
Article 361
Article 363
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following best describes the electoral system used to elect the President of India?
options: Proportional Representation
Proportional Representation and Single Transferable Vote System
First-Past-the-Post System
List System
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: In which one of the following situations does the President exercise genuine discretion?
options: Assenting to a Money Bill
Constituting a Finance Commission
Nominating twelve members to the Rajya Sabha
Appointing the Prime Minister when no party has a clear majority in the Lok Sabha
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about the Union Cabinet is NOT correct?
options: A person from outside Parliament can never be appointed to the Cabinet
It remains in power while it enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha
It is responsible to the Lok Sabha
It is the highest decision-making body of the executive
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following statements about the removal of the Vice-President is correct?
options: He is removed by impeachment like the President
He is removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by an effective majority and agreed to by the Lok Sabha, with no grounds specified
He can be removed by the President at pleasure
He is removed only by the Supreme Court
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which one of the following correctly describes the office of the Solicitor General of India?
options: It is a constitutional office created by Article 76
It is the highest law officer of the country
It is a statutory, non-constitutional office that assists the Attorney General
It is a member of the Union Cabinet
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Governor's pardoning power under Article 161 differs from the President's under Article 72 in that the Governor
options: can pardon offences under Union laws
can pardon a death sentence
has no pardoning power at all
cannot pardon a death sentence or a court-martial sentence, and deals only with offences against state laws
questions.subject: Polity
